scope_note: Covers the statutory powers of the Scottish Ministers to give directions to Health Boards (and Special Health Boards) in Scotland: the general power of direction, the specific intervention and default powers, and the general provisions governing how directions are made, varied and revoked. Limited to legislation (Acts and SIs); case law interpreting these powers is out of scope in this mode.

steps.title: Identify the primary Act governing Health Boards and the Ministers' relationship with them
steps.detail: Identify the principal Act constituting Health Boards and Special Health Boards in Scotland and conferring functions on them, and establish the basis on which those bodies exercise functions of the Scottish Ministers.

steps.title: Retrieve the general power of direction over Health Boards
steps.detail: Find the provision under which Health Boards must act subject to and in accordance with directions given by the Scottish Ministers, and establish its scope — which functions it reaches, and whether directions may be general or specific to a particular area or matter.

steps.title: Retrieve the specific intervention, default and failure powers
steps.detail: Find the provisions allowing the Scottish Ministers to intervene where a Health Board fails to carry out its functions or to provide a service to an acceptable standard, including any power to declare a body in default and any power to direct that its functions be performed by another body or person.

steps.title: Establish the general provisions governing directions
steps.detail: Find the general provision governing orders, regulations and directions under the Act — in particular whether directions may be varied or revoked, whether they may be exercised generally or in specified cases, and any procedural or publication requirements.

steps.title: Confirm that the powers are exercisable by the Scottish Ministers rather than a Minister of the Crown
steps.detail: Establish the devolution provisions under which functions conferred on the Secretary of State by the pre-devolution Act are now exercisable by the Scottish Ministers, and confirm the territorial extent and in-force status of the provisions relied on.
